hook_text: Everything from this term is hanging off one crane. Magnets, circuits, electromagnets, cranks, pulleys. Pull the string and watch them all work.
clip_script: Four shelves, one crane. Shelf one, magnets: two poles, like poles repel, and only ferrous metals stick, because their domains line up. That is why the crane sorts steel from copper. Shelf two, circuits: cell, switch, wire, bulb in a closed loop, drawn with a ruler and the right symbols. Shelf three, the electromagnet: current makes a field, the coil concentrates it, the iron core multiplies it, and the switch turns it off, so the crane can drop its load. Stronger with more turns, more current, soft iron. Shelf four, mechanisms: the crank is a second-class lever, handle over drum, about six. The pulley at the tip is a wheel and axle that just turns the pull, advantage one. Load over effort, paid for in distance. Forget a fact? Picture the crane and ask which part it is.
visual_style: Whiteboard crane with four labels lighting up in turn: magnet, circuit, coil, crank and pulley; short key phrases appearing beside each.
mood: Calm and confident, a term folding neatly into one picture.
pacing: Shelf, shelf, shelf, shelf, crane, each a few seconds.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and revise the term one shelf at a time.
